title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 185 (Loan to directors, etc.)

content.overview: Section 185 (as substituted) prohibits a company from directly or indirectly advancing any loan, including any loan represented by a book debt, or giving any guarantee or providing any security in connection with any loan taken by (a) any director of the company, or of a company which is its holding company, or any partner or relative of any such director; or (b) any firm in which any such director or relative is a partner. A loan may be advanced to any person in whom any of the directors is interested if a special resolution is passed with full disclosure in the explanatory statement and the loans are utilised for the principal business activities of the borrowing entity. Specified exceptions include loans to managing or whole-time directors as part of conditions of service extended to all employees or pursuant to a scheme approved by members, ordinary-course lending by companies whose ordinary business includes lending, and certain holding-company support to wholly owned subsidiaries used for principal business activities.
content.glance: Prohibition on loans/guarantees/security to directors, holding-company directors, their partners/relatives, and firms in which they are partners; special-resolution route for persons in whom a director is interested (principal-business use); limited statutory exceptions.
content.study: No company shall, directly or indirectly, advance any loan, including any loan represented by a book debt to, or give any guarantee or provide any security in connection with any loan taken by, (a) any director of company, or of a company which is its holding company or any partner or relative of any such director; or (b) any firm in which any such director or relative is a partner. A company may advance any loan or give any guarantee or provide any security in connection with any loan taken by any person in whom any of the directors of the company is interested subject to the condition that a special resolution is passed by the company in general meeting and the loans are utilised by the borrowing company for its principal business activities; the explanatory statement to the notice must disclose full particulars. Exceptions include: (i) loan to a managing or whole-time director as a part of the conditions of service extended by the company to all its employees or pursuant to any scheme approved by the members by a special resolution; (ii) a company which in the ordinary course of its business provides loans or gives guarantees or securities for the due repayment of any loan and in respect of such loans an interest is charged at a rate not less than the rate of prevailing yield of one year, three years, five years or ten years Government security closest to the tenor of the loan; (iii) any loan made by a holding company to its wholly owned subsidiary or any guarantee/security by a holding company in respect of a loan made to its wholly owned subsidiary, provided the loan is utilised for the principal business activities of the subsidiary. Private-company exemptions, if any, must be taken from the notification in force. Current-law framing: identify the borrower class; apply the prohibition; test special-resolution route; apply listed exceptions.

sections.heading: Core Prohibition
sections.body: No loan (including book debt), guarantee or security for a loan to a director of the company or of its holding company, or to a partner or relative of such director, or to a firm in which such director or relative is a partner.

sections.heading: Special-Resolution Route
sections.body: Loan/guarantee/security to a person in whom any director is interested may be given if a special resolution is passed with full particulars in the explanatory statement and the funds are used for the principal business activities of the borrower.

sections.heading: Exceptions
sections.body: MD/WTD loans under service conditions extended to all employees or member-approved scheme; ordinary-course lending at not less than prescribed Government-security yield; holding-company support to wholly owned subsidiary for principal business.

examples.title: Loan to director’s relative
examples.body: A company advances a loan to the spouse of a director. Section 185 prohibits loans to a relative of a director of the company, subject only to the special-resolution route or a listed exception if applicable.

examples.title: Wholly owned subsidiary support
examples.body: A holding company guarantees a loan taken by its wholly owned subsidiary for the subsidiary’s principal business. That support falls within the statutory exception under s. 185.

hypotheticals.question: Does calling a prohibited director loan a matter of internal management save it?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 185 is a statutory prohibition. Labelling the transaction as internal management does not displace the prohibition or the need to fit an exception or the special-resolution route.

distinctions.title: Loan to directors (s. 185) vs inter-corporate loans and investments (s. 186)
distinctions.left: Prohibition focused on directors and connected persons
distinctions.right: Limits and approvals for loans, guarantees and investments to other bodies corporate

misconceptions.trap: Any loan to a director is allowed if the Board approves it.
misconceptions.correction: Board approval alone is not enough. The transaction must fit a statutory exception or the special-resolution route with principal-business use; otherwise it is prohibited.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 185 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify borrower class. II. Apply prohibition. III. Test special-resolution route. IV. Apply listed exceptions. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Borrower facts; prohibition; exception or special resolution; precise relief.

examTips: Special resolution + principal-business use for persons in whom a director is interested.
Private-company exemptions only if a notification so provides.
